summary.text: Euler's formula says the complex exponential function is eⁱˣ = cos x + i sin x, tying exponentials to trigonometry.
It appears throughout mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering, and Richard Feynman called it the most remarkable formula in mathematics.
Euler derived it around 1740 by comparing series expansions of the exponential and trigonometric expressions, and it was first published in 1748.

facts.label: First published
facts.value: 1748, in Euler's Introductio in analysin infinitorum

facts.label: Unit circle
facts.value: It traces the unit circle in the complex plane

facts.label: Short name
facts.value: Sometimes written cis x, for cosine plus i sine

items.prompt: A textbook shortens the complex exponential to the three letters cis. What do they stand for?

options.label: Circle, inverse, square
Cosine, inverse, sine
Cosine divided by i sine
Cosine plus i sine

items.explain: The name cis x is short for cosine plus i sine.

items.prompt: In Euler's formula the angle runs steadily through the real numbers. Where does the resulting number travel in the complex plane?

options.label: Back and forth along the real axis
Around a circle of radius one
Outward along a growing spiral
Straight up the imaginary axis

items.explain: The result is a unit complex number that traces out the unit circle as the angle varies.

items.prompt: A student says Euler's formula only works when the angle x is an ordinary real number. Is that right?

options.label: No, it stays valid when x is a number with an i part too
Yes, any imaginary part makes both sides meaningless
Yes, but only for angles that are whole numbers
No, but only when x is exactly 0 or π

items.explain: The formula is still valid if x is a complex number, and it is also called Euler's formula in that more general case.

items.prompt: Set x = π in Euler's formula. What value does the complex exponential take?

options.label: Zero
One
The imaginary unit

items.explain: At x = π the formula gives e^iπ = −1, known as Euler's identity.

items.prompt: Real logarithms give one answer for each positive number. What is different about the logarithm of a complex number?

options.label: It always comes out as a purely real number
It can only be defined on the unit circle
It has exactly two values, like a square root
It can have infinitely many values

items.explain: A complex logarithm is multi-valued: its values differ by multiples of 2πi.

items.prompt: Around 1740, Euler turned to the exponential function. What method led him to the equation?

options.label: Measuring angles of triangles drawn in a circle
Solving a problem about electric circuits
Comparing series expansions of the exponential and trig functions
Plotting complex numbers as points in a plane

items.explain: He derived the equation by comparing the series expansions of the exponential and trigonometric expressions. The plane picture was described later by Caspar Wessel.
